selection.method: highest remaining verified actor-primary profiles after Batch 22

profiles.name: James Stevens
profiles.excerpt: James Stevens was a New York radio repertory actor whose surviving work is strongest in X Minus One and Johnny Dollar.
profiles.bio_html:
James Stevens worked in the New York radio repertory during the 1950s and 1960s, when science fiction and detective drama offered some of the last regular outlets for network actors. His credits show a performer moving between realistic crime stories and speculative material.

Stevens appeared repeatedly on X Minus One and Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar, with additional work on Duffy's Tavern and Theater Five. That range placed him in both established network formats and the later efforts to keep dramatic radio alive.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves nine X Minus One performances credited to Stevens, seven Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar appearances, and one broadcast each on Duffy's Tavern and Theater Five.

profiles.name: Jerry Farber
profiles.excerpt: Jerry Farber was a supporting radio actor whose surviving work centers on NBC University Theater and extends into comedy, detective and Hollywood anthology drama.
profiles.bio_html:
Jerry Farber belonged to the professional supporting repertory heard across postwar network radio. His surviving credits show regular work in literary adaptation as well as comedy and detective programs.

NBC University Theater became the strongest concentration of Farber's work, while The Great Gildersleeve, Let George Do It, Lux Radio Theatre, Screen Directors Playhouse and The Adventures of Philip Marlowe placed him in very different production styles.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves ten NBC University Theater performances credited to Farber, two The Great Gildersleeve appearances and additional broadcasts across several major dramatic series.

profiles.name: Julie Bennett
profiles.excerpt: Julie Bennett began in radio as a teenager and developed the vocal versatility that later made her a prolific animation voice actress.
profiles.bio_html:
Julie Bennett was born in Manhattan in 1932 and grew up in Los Angeles, where she began professional acting while still in her teens. Radio and theatre were among her earliest professional outlets before television and voice work broadened her career.

Bennett became known for a strong ear for accents and dialects, a skill that served her in radio drama and later animation. She eventually voiced Cindy Bear and many other cartoon characters, carrying microphone technique learned in radio into a long voice-acting career.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves seven The Phil Harris-Alice Faye Show performances credited to Bennett, five The Railroad Hour appearances and additional work on Barrie Craig, Crime Classics, Lux Radio Theatre, Sears Radio Theater, The Great Gildersleeve and The Whistler.

profiles.name: Kerry Jordan
profiles.excerpt: Kerry Jordan became a major South African radio actor after stage and screen work abroad, and is especially remembered as Dr. Watson opposite Graham Armitage’s Sherlock Holmes.
profiles.bio_html:
Kerry Jordan was born in New Zealand and trained for the stage after earlier work in broadcasting and several years of legal study. He worked in Britain before moving to South Africa in the 1960s, where radio became a substantial part of his career.

Jordan's best-remembered microphone role was Dr. Watson opposite Graham Armitage in Springbok Radio's The Stories of Sherlock Holmes. His broader South African career also included stage, television and extensive radio drama.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 18 The Stories of Sherlock Holmes performances credited to Jordan, documenting his Watson as one of the later international radio interpretations of Conan Doyle's character.

profiles.name: Lee Millar Sr.
profiles.excerpt: Lee Millar Sr. was a stage and radio actor whose Hollywood microphone work led into Disney voice acting, including an early run as the voice of Pluto.
profiles.bio_html:
Lee Carson Millar Sr. was born in Oakland in 1888 and worked professionally on stage before radio and animation expanded his career. He married actress Verna Felton, and their son Lee Millar Jr. later became an actor in his own right.

Millar became a dependable supporting player on Lux Radio Theatre during the 1930s, often handling smaller character parts around major film stars. He also performed voice work for Disney and was among the early performers to voice Pluto.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 18 Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to the source name Lee Millar. His public profile uses Lee Millar Sr. so his work remains distinct from that of his son.

profiles.name: Rex Harrison
profiles.excerpt: Rex Harrison brought his polished stage persona to radio as the star of The Private Files of Rex Saunders, a brief 1951 detective series built around his voice and wit.
profiles.bio_html:
Rex Harrison was born in Lancashire in 1908 and became one of the leading British stage actors of his generation before major film roles made him internationally famous. His crisp diction and controlled irony were as distinctive on microphone as they were onstage.

Radio gave Harrison a continuing detective vehicle in The Private Files of Rex Saunders, where he played an urbane investigator assisted by Alec, voiced by Leon Janney. The series ran briefly on NBC in 1951 and adapted Harrison's sophisticated screen persona to mystery radio.

Golden Radio Hour preserves 14 recordings of The Private Files of Rex Saunders and also holds Harrison appearances on Academy Award Theater, Duffy's Tavern, Lux Radio Theatre and The Big Show.

profiles.name: Ross Martin
profiles.excerpt: Ross Martin brought a remarkable command of accents and languages to radio before becoming widely known as Artemus Gordon on The Wild Wild West.
profiles.bio_html:
Ross Martin was born Martin Rosenblatt in Poland in 1920 and grew up in New York. Gifted with languages and dialects, he developed a performing career in radio, stage, film and television.

Radio used that vocal flexibility across adventure, science fiction and espionage programs. Martin appeared on John Steele, Adventurer, Dimension X, X Minus One and Cloak and Dagger before television made him famous as master-of-disguise Artemus Gordon.

Golden Radio Hour currently verifies seven John Steele, Adventurer performances credited to Martin, two each on Dimension X and X Minus One, and additional appearances on CBS Radio Mystery Theater, Cloak and Dagger and Stroke of Fate.

profiles.name: Tom Brown
profiles.excerpt: Tom Brown was a film and radio character actor whose surviving GRH work ranges from Lux Radio Theatre and FBI drama to The Saint and The Whistler.
profiles.bio_html:
Tom Brown built a long acting career that began in film while he was still young and expanded into radio and television. Radio drew on the same straightforward character style that kept him working steadily in screen supporting roles.

His surviving microphone credits cross film adaptation, crime and mystery, including Lux Radio Theatre, This Is Your FBI, The Saint, The Whistler and the later Sears Radio Theater.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves four performances each on Lux Radio Theatre, Sears Radio Theater and This Is Your FBI credited to Brown, three The Saint appearances and two The Whistler broadcasts.

profiles.name: Betty Harford
profiles.excerpt: Betty Harford was a British-born actress whose American radio work became especially strong in Crime Classics before a long television career.
profiles.bio_html:
Betty Harford was born in England and built an acting career in the United States across radio, stage, film and television. Her clear delivery and flexibility made her a strong fit for historical and anthology drama.

She appeared repeatedly on Crime Classics, where Elliott Lewis's productions required actors to move among different periods, accents and social worlds from week to week. Her later television career included recurring and guest roles across several decades.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 12 Crime Classics performances credited to Harford, two Escape appearances and additional broadcasts on Lux Radio Theatre, NBC University Theater and Sears Radio Theater.

profiles.name: Constance Cavendish
profiles.excerpt: Constance Cavendish was a stage-trained radio actress whose surviving work is concentrated in NBC University Theater and other prestige dramatic anthologies.
profiles.bio_html:
Constance Cavendish worked in the professional radio repertory that handled literary adaptation and serious anthology drama during the postwar years. Her surviving credits place her most often in productions that demanded formal stage technique and careful handling of language.

NBC University Theater became the strongest concentration of her work, supplemented by Escape, Lux Radio Theatre and The Whistler. That combination shows an actress moving between prestige literature and suspense without relying on a recurring character.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 11 NBC University Theater performances credited to Cavendish, three Escape appearances, two Lux Radio Theatre broadcasts and one The Whistler episode.
